title: Introduce circuit checkpointing and autorestore hotpatch for transient regional egress spikes
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Hotpatch: add circuit checkpointing and autorestore to reduce flip-flapping during transient egress/egress-surge events; adds SLO backfill to avoid immediate penalties for short-lived circuit flips.
description:
Motivation: We observed an incident where short-lived regional egress surges (SUP-7822) caused circuits to flip into degraded states and then immediately reopen, generating noisy SLO violations and unstable routing during recovery. This PR implements a lightweight checkpoint-and-restore mechanism to preserve healthy circuit state and automatically restore on stable conditions, plus an SLO backfill to avoid penalizing brief transient flips.

What this PR does:
- Introduces circuit checkpoints at controlled stabilization points so we can restore a recent healthy state instead of leaving the system in a degraded sticky state after a noisy failure.
- Adds an autorestore controller that attempts a safe restore when probe results and rolling latency/err-rate windows stabilize. Restores are rate-limited and hysteresis-protected.
- Implements an SLO backfill window: when a circuit flap is detected and subsequently autorestored within the backfill window (configurable, default 60s), telemetry will tag events as transient and backfill SLO counters to prevent users from seeing immediate regression.
- Adds telemetry: new metrics and structured traces for checkpoint create/restore/expire decisions and restore rationale (probe scores, KV pressure, egress delta).
- Adds unit and integration tests that simulate regional egress spikes and verify that checkpoints/restore prevent long-lived degraded routing and that SLOs are backfilled as expected.

Risks and mitigations:
- Restore could hide real persistent failures if incorrectly triggered. Mitigation: restore requires a composite probe score (latency + error rate + kv-pressure) and a minimal stabilization window; restores are rate-limited and only attempted on circuits with recent healthy checkpoints.
- Added logic touches the runtime stabilization path; change set is guarded behind a runtime flag (runtime.features.circuit_checkpointing) and feature rollout is staged via canary.

Rollout plan:
1) Deploy to canary cluster behind feature flag. Observe checkpoint/restore metrics and SLO backfill tags for 48 hours.
2) Expand canary to 10% regional traffic if no anomalous restores observed.
3) Full rollout and telemetry-driven adjustments to backfill window and probe thresholds.

Checklist:
- [x] Implementation in runtime (checkpoint + restore controller)
- [x] Telemetry/trace additions and tagging for SLO backfill
- [x] Unit tests for checkpoint lifecycle
- [x] Integration test simulating egress spike and verifying restore and backfill behavior
- [x] Helm config toggle and defaults added
- [x] SRE + Runtime review approvals

Related: ENG-4275 (circuit stabilization follow-up), ENG-4291 (telemetry tagging for transient events).
